subject: Clarify PHI dataflow, DLP controls, and BAA applicability for PatientSync integration
messages:
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@patientsync.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: PatientSync Security <security@patientsync.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PHI scope question for PatientSync integration

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed to contract and a BAA review, our security team has a few clarifying questions about what components of the PatientSync workload would be considered PHI (if any) when routed through Redwood’s hosted API vs. Dedicated/Private deployments. High-level asks below: 

1) In typical webhook + file-upload workflows, does Redwood persist any user-provided content (payload bodies, transcripts, attachments) beyond request-level logs? If so, how long and where?
2) Does Redwood’s prefix/KV cache ever store full user content (e.g., patient notes) or only model keys/embeddings? What controls exist for TTL and encryption?
3) We run downstream analytics and IDS on anonymized telemetry — could telemetry include PHI in any of the default logs or traces?
4) If we need a BAA, which deployment options (Hosted with BAA, Dedicated, Private) are supported and what evidence do you provide (dataflow diagram, DLP controls, retention snapshots)?

Appreciate concise answers we can share with our legal/security teams. If it helps, I can share a sample sanitized payload.

Thanks,
Olivia Turner
Head of Security Operations
PatientSync

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@patientsync.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI scope question for PatientSync integration

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then I’ll attach a single-page dataflow + DLP summary for your security team and loop in our compliance lead.

1) Persistence: Redwood’s hosted API does not persist customer request payloads beyond short-lived operational logs by default. Logs are truncated and retained 7 days in hosted by default; Dedicated/Private options allow configuring retention or disabling request payload logging entirely.

2) KV/prefix cache: The runtime stores KV cache entries (decoder keys, attention caches) but not full original request bodies. Customers may enable prefix caching of prompt prefixes; if you enable customer-side prefix caching we can provide a policy that avoids storing raw PHI. TTLs are configurable per-namespace; entries are encrypted at rest and keys are customer-controlled for Dedicated/Private with KMS integration.

3) Telemetry: Default telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) does not include user text. Trace sampling can include small excerpts when debugging is explicitly enabled; we recommend disabling debug sampling for PHI traffic. We provide a telemetry scrubber and DLP hooks to filter PII/PHI out of traces.

4) BAA & deployment: We will sign a BAA for customers that require HIPAA coverage. Both Dedicated and Private clearly support PHI-handling with customer KMS and configurable retention. Hosted can be covered under a BAA if specific controls and retention are agreed in the contract — our security team will produce a scoped evidence package (dataflow diagram, retention policy, DLP control matrix, sample audit logs).

I’ve attached a 1-page dataflow diagram and a DLP controls summary. Looping in Naomi for evidence and specific retention windows.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png (image/png, 128KB); redwood-dlp-controls-summary.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fw: PHI scope question for PatientSync integration — evidence packet prep

Team —

PatientSync asked for explicit confirmation on what is stored, where telemetry may contain PHI, and what artifacts we can provide for a BAA. I propose the following deliverables to send as a single package: 

- Dataflow diagram (attached) annotated with: ingress endpoints, model runtime, KV cache TTLs, and egress to analytics.
- DLP controls summary (attached) that lists scrubbers, regex rules, and scrubbed vs. raw log policies.
- Sample audit snapshot: 24-hr logging slice with sensitive fields redacted (sample-logging-snapshot.txt).
- Short note on Deployment options: Hosted with scoped retention (7d default, configurable), Dedicated with customer KMS and retention by policy, Private on-prem option.

Questions: Can we provide a 3rd-party SOC2 control mapping for the logs item for their legal team? Also confirm whether we can commit to disabling trace excerpts for the contract if they require.

Marissa — please help format the packet for external consumption and include a single-line summary for legal. Dev — please confirm the scrubber regex coverage and whether telemetry export adapters ever include request bodies in any default configuration.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@patientsync.com>
Cc: PatientSync Security <security@patientsync.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI scope question for PatientSync integration — evidence packet

Olivia —

Thanks again for the questions. Attached is the packet we discussed: dataflow diagram (shows where request bodies may pass through), DLP controls summary (regex and scrubber behavior), and a redacted sample logging snapshot. Highlights: 

- Hosted default: request payloads not persisted beyond operational logs; operational logs are redacted and retained 7 days unless contractually extended. We will disable debug trace excerpts for your tenant as part of the BAA.
- KV/prefix cache: does not contain full original user files by default; caching of prompt prefixes can be disabled per-tenant. Cache entries are encrypted at rest.
- Telemetry: default telemetry contains no user text; debug sampling must be opt-in and will be disabled in your production tenant.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 control mapping for logging and monitoring controls and a scoped signing of a BAA. Dedicated or Private deployments provide stronger isolation and customer-managed KMS if you require it.

Next steps: please confirm which deployment you prefer (Hosted with scoped BAA | Dedicated | Private). If Hosted with BAA, confirm required retention window for logs and whether you want us to disable debug trace sampling (we recommend disabling). Marissa from our team will follow up with a one-page legal summary for your counsel.

Best,
Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png; redwood-dlp-controls-summary.pdf; sample-logging-snapshot.txt
